newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's Hrawi denies threatening resignation.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's Hrawi denies threatening resignation.

text.p: Lebanon's President Elias Hrawi denied newspaper reports that he threatened to resign after the government withdrew a local elections bill from parliament, causing concern that it might postpone the vote due in summer.
In a news conference on Wednesday night, Hrawi said: "The talk of resignation and going home and things of the sort is just talk. I protect the constitution and it protects me".
Beirut newspapers last week quoted named visitors to Hrawi, including members of parliament, as saying he told them he would resign if the municipal and mayoral elections were not held as scheduled.

They quoted Hrawi as complaining that Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and parliament Speaker Nabih Berri had infringed the constitution by withdrawing the bill for re-drafting, saying government drafts could only be withdrawn on presidential authority.

Hrawi told the news conference he believed the elections would "strengthen the bases of the state" because all Christian opposition groups, including those which have boycotted national elections since the civil war, had decided to take part.

However, he said he would accept parliament's decision if it decided against holding the elections. "If the absolute majority at the parliament says no to the elections then I will sumbit to that," he said.
The elections, which will be Lebanon's first local polls since 1963, are scheduled for June 1 and 8.
